problems.title: A nonrepeating prefix followed by a repeating block
problems.question: Convert 0.19(199) to a fraction.
problems.idea: Subtract the nonrepeating prefix after aligning the repeated blocks.
steps: Here the numerator is 19199-19=19180 and the denominator 100·999=99900.
Reduce by 20.

problems.title: A terminating decimal needs only primes 2 and 5
problems.question: Which listed fraction has a nonterminating decimal?
problems.idea: Reduce denominators first.
formulas: A reduced fraction terminates iff its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5.
steps: 4/375 is reduced and its denominator contains prime 3.
By contrast, 6/375 reduces to 2/125, and the other listed denominators use only 2 and 5.

problems.title: Two tails of an absolute-value inequality
problems.question: Solve |2x-3|>3.
problems.idea: The inner expression is either above 3 or below -3.
formulas: |u|>c iff u>c or u<-c, for c≥0.
steps: 2x-3>3 gives x>3.
2x-3<-3 gives x<0.

problems.title: A single strict linear inequality cannot make a bounded interval
problems.question: Which listed set cannot be the solutions of ax>b with real parameters a,b?
problems.idea: Classify the cases a>0,a<0,a=0.
formulas: For a≠0 the set is one open half-line; for a=0 it is ℝ or ∅.
steps: A bounded interval such as (1,3) is none of those possibilities.

problems.title: Equal transformed values determine four numbers
problems.question: Four numbers sum to 64. Multiplying the first by 3, dividing the second by 3, adding 3 to the third and subtracting 3 from the fourth gives equal values. Find the difference of the two least original numbers.
problems.idea: Let every transformed value be t.
steps: Their sum is (16/3)t=64, so t=12.
The numbers are 4,36,9,15.
The two least differ by 9-4=5.

problems.title: The negative sign survives radical simplification
problems.question: Simplify -√(-a³) over the reals.
problems.idea: Its domain is a≤0.
steps: Since a≤0, |a|=-a.
Therefore -√(-a³)=-(-a)√(-a)=a√(-a).

problems.title: Two whole secants with proportional inner parts
problems.question: Two secants from an exterior point have whole lengths 4,6 and inner parts in ratio 1:4. Find the smaller exterior part.
problems.idea: Use equal powers of the exterior point.
steps: Put the inner lengths t,4t, so external lengths are 4-t,6-4t.
Then 4(4-t)=6(6-4t), giving t=1.
The exterior lengths are 3 and 2. Reversing which secant has the fourfold inner part gives a negative t and is impossible.

problems.title: A doubled angle and a bisector length
problems.question: In ABC, BD is a bisector of length 2,AD=1 and B=2C. Find BC.
problems.idea: Triangle BCD is isosceles because DBC=C.
steps: Let BC=t, so AB=t/2.
The bisector identity gives 4=t²/2-2.
Thus t²=12 and the positive length is 2√3.

problems.title: Three equal consecutive circle chords
problems.question: A cyclic trapezoid has leg AB equal to smaller base BC. CD=6 and minor arc CD=60°. Find the distance between diagonal midpoints.
problems.idea: A cyclic trapezoid is isosceles.
formulas: AB=BC=CD=6; equal chords have equal minor arcs.
steps: The consecutive arcs AB,BC,CD each measure 60°.
The remaining arc AD is 180°, so AD is a diameter. Since a 60° chord equals the radius, AD=12.
The diagonal-midpoint distance is half the base difference: (12-6)/2=3.

problems.title: A midpoint parallelogram can also collapse
problems.question: N,P are midpoints of BC,AD; M,K of diagonals AC,BD. Which listed assertion about MNKP is false?
problems.idea: Use vector differences between consecutive midpoints.
formulas: MN=AB/2 and NK=CD/2 as vectors, with opposite sides reversed.
steps: When nondegenerate, MNKP is a parallelogram, with adjacent side lengths AB/2,CD/2. Those lengths need not be equal, so it need not be a rhombus.
Suitable original side directions and lengths can make it a rectangle, rhombus or square.
If AB∥CD, these four midpoint points can instead be collinear or coincide.
problems.answer: The intended false assertion is “necessarily a rhombus.”
problems.note: The claim “necessarily a parallelogram” also needs a nondegeneracy qualification. For a rectangle ABCD, M=K and all four midpoints here lie on one line.

problems.title: Two angle bisectors meet on the larger base
problems.question: A right trapezoid has perpendicular leg AB=6 and D=30°. The B,C bisectors meet at P on the larger base AD. Find AD.
problems.idea: Find AP and PD using two isosceles triangles.
formulas: B=90° gives AP=AB=6; C=150° gives PCD=75°.
steps: In triangle PCD the other angles are D=30°,P=75°, so PD=CD.
The slanted leg is CD=AB/sin30°=12.
Therefore AD=AP+PD=6+12=18.

problems.title: Identify the nonsquare radicand
problems.question: Which is irrational among √784,√841,√876,√961,√1024,√1089?
problems.idea: Check the nearby integer squares.
steps: 876 lies strictly between 29²=841 and 30²=900 and is not a square.
The square root of a positive nonsquare integer is irrational.

problems.title: Combine a nonnegative coefficient with a radical
problems.question: Simplify -x√(-x) over the reals.
problems.idea: The domain x≤0 makes -x nonnegative.
steps: The radicand is -x³.

problems.title: Power of an interior chord point
problems.question: A chord of length 6.5 contains M, with AM:MB=9:4 and OM=4. Find the circle radius.
problems.idea: Use the product of the chord pieces.
steps: Thus 9=R²-16.
So R²=25 and R=5.

problems.title: A tangent is one leg of a right triangle
problems.question: A is distance 5 from a radius-3 circle centre. Find the tangent segment from A.
problems.idea: The radius to the contact is perpendicular to the tangent.
steps: The length is √(25-9)=4.

problems.title: Both inequalities lose their x terms
problems.question: Find all a for which a(x+2)-x≥(a-1)x+2 and (a-2)x+a<ax+19-2x hold for every real x.
problems.idea: Simplify both sides before comparing coefficients.
steps: The x coefficients already match in each inequality.
Thus the necessary and sufficient parameter conditions are a≥1 and a<19.

problems.title: Integer endpoints inside a strict interval
problems.question: For 2|x+1|<5+x, find greatest integer solution minus least integer solution.
problems.idea: Solve the two sign branches.
steps: The combined interval is (-7/3,3).
Its integer solutions are -2,-1,0,1,2.
Their extreme difference is 2-(-2)=4.

problems.title: A midpoint expressed with half-diagonal vectors
problems.question: Parallelogram diagonals meet at O, AC=24,BD=8,COD=60°. Find the distance from D to the midpoint of BC.
problems.idea: Use O as vector origin.
steps: The midpoint of BC is (c-d)/2. Its vector from D is (c-3d)/2.
The squared length is (144+9·16-6·24)/4=36.

problems.title: Equal-height circle points fix the tangency abscissa
problems.question: A circle passes through the midpoints of hypotenuse AB and leg BC of right ABC, and touches leg AC at M. Find CM:MA.
formulas: The two known circle points are (a/2,b/2),(0,b/2).
steps: Their perpendicular bisector is x=a/4, so the circle centre has that x-coordinate.
Tangency to AC, the x-axis, puts M=(a/4,0).
Thus CM=a/4 and MA=3a/4.

problems.title: Count lattice points under three strict bounds
problems.question: Count natural-coordinate points with x+y<4, y<3x,3y>x.
problems.idea: List the positive pairs satisfying the first bound.
steps: All three satisfy both remaining strict inequalities.
Points on either coordinate axis fail one of those inequalities, so allowing zero would not add any.

problems.title: Square-root inequality with its domain
problems.question: Solve √(3x-9)<6.
problems.idea: Require the radicand to be nonnegative before squaring.
steps: The lower bound gives x≥3 and the upper gives x<15.

problems.title: Midpoints of two medians
problems.question: One triangle side has length a. Find the distance between the midpoints of the medians to the other two sides.
problems.idea: Write the two midpoint positions using vertex vectors.
steps: Subtract to get U-V=(B-C)/4.
The length is one quarter of BC.

problems.title: A small isosceles triangle at a median midpoint
problems.question: A=40°,AB=2AC. N∈AB with AN:NB=1:3, and M is midpoint of BC. Find BNM.
problems.idea: Let K be the midpoint of AB.
steps: Thus NK=KM. At K, the angle NKM is 180°-A=140°.
The two base angles of NKM are (180°-140°)/2=20°.
Since NB follows NK, BNM=KNM=20°.

problems.title: Subtract conjugate reciprocal radicals
problems.question: Which listed expression is rational?
problems.idea: Rationalize the pair involving √7±2.
steps: The numerator is -4 and the denominator 3.
The result is -4/3, rational; the other listed expressions retain nonzero irrational radicals.

problems.title: Intersect two linear inequalities
problems.question: Solve 2(1-2x)+3≤6-7(x-2), and -(2+3x)<3(4x-1)-14.
problems.idea: Simplify each condition.
steps: The first gives x≤5.
The second gives x>1.
Their intersection is (1,5].
